questions.question: Where are you most likely to have a collision?

options.text: At an intersection.
When riding in a group.
On the expressway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection.
questions.explanation: Intersections have the most potential for conflicts between you and other traffic.

questions.question: When riding ________, you face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles.

options.text: On the expressway
Near an intersection
In a group

questions.correctAnswerText: Near an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles. Position your motorcycle in your lane to be as visible as possible to other drivers.

questions.question: There is usually an oily strip in the center of a traffic lane. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease buildup.
Not worry about the oil and grease buildup.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease buildup.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease buildup.
questions.explanation: Stay away from the oily strip. The buildup is usually only about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it while staying in the center portion of your lane.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: The mirrors give you a complete view.
The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
The mirrors should only be used when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Means they see you.
Does not mean they will yield to you properly.
Guarantees they will yield to you properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will yield to you properly.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers sometimes look directly at motorcyclists but still fail to see them.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:

options.text: In front of the operator.
Sidesaddle.
Behind the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the operator and hold onto the operator's waist or hips. They can also hold handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: One danger of riding directly next to another vehicle is:

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can easily see you.
You may not be able to read roadside signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could swerve into your lane or block your way if you need to escape a hazard.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between you and other vehicles?

options.text: At an intersection
On the highway
On any road

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest potential for conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Speed up.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before turning. Taking a turn too fast can cause you to veer out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: If a motorcyclist cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, they should:

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Approach the obstacle at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the obstacle at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: How should you position yourself to control a motorcycle properly?

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent so you can steer easily. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you balance during turns.

questions.question: What should you know about taking over-the-counter medication before riding?

options.text: It is usually fine because over-the-counter medications are weak.
It is always acceptable.
It may affect your riding ability and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may affect your riding ability and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how a new medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: When can you use a motorized bicycle or moped in a bicycle lane?

options.text: Never. You cannot use motorized bicycles in bicycle lanes.
Only when you are carrying a passenger.
Only if local law or law enforcement allows it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if local law or law enforcement allows it.
questions.explanation: You can use motorized bicycles and mopeds in bicycle lanes only if your local area permits it.

questions.question: What should you do when stopping your motorcycle with a passenger?

options.text: Ride faster than you normally would.
Start slowing down earlier than you normally would.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than you normally would.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight makes your motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger gaps when entering or crossing traffic.

questions.question: What should you look for in a motorcycle protective jacket?

options.text: Black or another dark color.
Warmth.
Leather or synthetic materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather or synthetic materials.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket that covers your arms completely and fits snugly but allows you to move freely. Leather or sturdy synthetic materials with body armor offer the best protection.

questions.question: Which lane position best prevents other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from squeezing into your lane. It also makes you more visible in a car's rearview mirror.

questions.question: How should you secure a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: Secure it as low as possible.
Secure it as high as possible.
Attach it to a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure it as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Loads should be secured as low as possible. Attaching a load to a sissy bar raises your motorcycle's center of gravity and hurts its balance.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to work properly?

options.text: Fasten securely.
Block your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Prevent eyeglasses or sunglasses from being worn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist breaking, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses.

questions.question: What should you check when choosing a helmet?

options.text: It has no cracks or defects.
It looks nice.
It fits loosely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and be free of cracks, loose padding, and frayed straps.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: On the highway.
At intersections.
On rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles have the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles. Be extra careful when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: When a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the motorcyclist should:

options.text: Increase their following distance.
Decrease their following distance.
Keep the same following distance as usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase their following distance.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle towing a trailer needs more time to stop because of the added weight. You should increase your following distance.

questions.question: The front brake should:

options.text: Only be used in an emergency.
Be used together with the rear brake.
Not be used because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Most motorcycle and car accidents happen:

options.text: At intersections.
On open roads.
In parking lots.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Most crashes between motorcycles and cars happen at intersections. Usually, the car driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket, it should:

options.text: Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Not be made of leather or other sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket made of leather or another sturdy material. It should fit snugly enough to not flap in the wind, but loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger.
Are required for both the driver and passenger.
Are not required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have passenger footrests. Good footing keeps your passenger from falling off and pulling you off too.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.

options.text: Louder than
Quieter than
About the same volume as

questions.correctAnswerText: Quieter than
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as car horns. Use your horn when needed, but do not depend on it to keep you safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles are entering the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let all crossing traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when safe.

questions.question: When being passed, motorcyclists should ride in which part of their lane?

options.text: The right side
The center
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the other driver creates danger for both of you.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use both the front and rear brakes together and downshift.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually best to:

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Usually, it is safest to ride straight within your lane when crossing angled railroad or trolley tracks. Changing your angle may push you into another lane and cause a crash with oncoming traffic.
